title: Intel Terafab deal survives TSMC takeover rumours ...
key_facts: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan confirmed the Terafab arrangement on Wednesday (7 Oct).
Musk rejected the idea that TSMC would take control; his companies would build and operate the facility, with TSMC potentially subleasing part.
Terafab is meant to secure advanced chip supply for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, using Intel's 14A process.
Intel has not detailed the commercial structure, and no committed wafer volumes or financial terms are disclosed.
SpaceX is to build the first phase in Grimes County, Texas, with more than $16.8 billion of capital investment and 3,000 jobs.
No agreement for TSMC participation has been announced.
quote_evidence: The Intel Terafab deal remains in place despite several days of speculation that TSMC could displace Intel from Elon Musk's semiconductor manufacturing project.
He said the facility would be built and operated by his companies, with TSMC potentially subleasing only part of the site.
No agreement for TSMC participation in Terafab has been announced.
why_it_matters_hint: Narrows the TSMC-takeover rumour; Intel stays; operating control with Musk.
notes: Follow-up of 1007:X16 (Bloomberg: Intel keeps working on Terafab) and of item 36 in the 4 Oct 2026 edition (TSMC talks, Tom's Hardware citing Culpium). New today: Musk's statement that his companies will operate the site. Full text read.
